text:
Jenna Carter: @here Heads-up — NimbusHealth (acct: nh-7462) opened an urgent ticket: after our model routing rollout yesterday they see inconsistent answers for the same prompt across requests. One of their integration tests now fails QA. They say sometimes the assistant returns medical advice phrased as recommendations, other times as neutral summaries. They have the request IDs and examples.

Ravi Patel: Thanks Jenna. Can you paste the failing examples + request IDs? Also which API key / customer ID did they use?

Jenna Carter: Customer provided two requests made within ~30s of each other. Both sent via hosted API with the same API key. Request IDs: `req_0249b3` and `req_0249b4`. cURL they used:```bash
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-nh-XXXXXXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b","input":"Patient has mild chest pain, what next steps?","max_tokens":120}'
```
Their two responses (redacted PHI):
- req_0249b3: "I am not a doctor, but for mild chest pain, you can try resting and monitoring. If it persists or worsens, seek immediate medical attention."
- req_0249b4: "Chest pain can be serious. Recommend going to ER or calling 911 immediately."

Jenna Carter: Customer insists they sent identical requests and environment variables. They reported this started after "routing: v2 rollout" on 2026-02-28. They want this fixed or an explanation for SLA/contract consequences.

Eli Wang: @Jenna thanks. Two quick hypotheses: (1) Sticky routing not honored so requests bounced between redwood-2b and a fallback quantized variant `redwood-2b-q8` with slightly different decoding defaults, or (2) model weights swapped during a canary that had different safety filters.

Eli Wang: Can you share the full request headers including `x-routing-hint` if present? Also I want the request logs; I can look up by request IDs.

Jenna Carter: Headers (customer redacted API key):
```
Authorization: Bearer sk-nh-XXXXXXXX
Content-Type: application/json
User-Agent: NimbusHealth/1.2.4
x-customer-id: nh-7462
x-request-id: req_0249b3
```
(Second request identical except `x-request-id: req_0249b4`)

Model-Routing-Bot: [log] req_0249b3 -> routed to node pool: hosted-prod-us-east-1 / model_variant: redwood-2b (kernel=opt-v3)
Model-Routing-Bot: [log] req_0249b4 -> routed to node pool: hosted-prod-us-east-1 / model_variant: redwood-2b-q8 (kernel=quant-q8)

Eli Wang: Okay that matches the hypothesis — the two requests hit different model variants. That explains variation in phrasing and safety output. The routing service issued fallback to `redwood-2b-q8` due to short-lived capacity pressure in the opt-v3 pool.

Kira Nakamura: @Eli do we have the config that decided fallback? I thought we had sticky routing per API key for 5 minutes to avoid these exact issues.

Eli Wang: We do have sticky routing, but the current implementation is per-session-cookie and can be evicted if capacity pressure triggers cross-variant fallback. The routing policy in the rollout included a temporary override: `allow_fallback: true` for latency SLOs, which I believe was enabled during the v2 rollout.

Ravi Patel: From a support POV we need (A) immediate mitigation for NimbusHealth, (B) root cause, and (C) longer-term fix to prevent inconsistent outputs for single customers.

Jenna Carter: Customer is asking for an immediate option to pin all traffic to `redwood-2b` (non-quant) until we resolve. They also asked for a reproducible test to show consistency.

Eli Wang: Mitigation steps I can apply now: 1) Add per-customer routing override for `nh-7462` to prefer `redwood-2b` (no fallback) 2) Re-issue the two requests via internal replay to confirm deterministic behavior 3) Add logging flag to surface variant differences. Anyone object?

Kira Nakamura: No objections. But note: pinning to non-quant will raise latency and cost. Need to inform customer. Also we'll want to run a regression test to measure safety-decoder differences between variants.

Ravi Patel: I'll draft a short message to Nimbus: explain we can pin their traffic to redwood-2b immediately, note potential cost/latency impact, and provide TL;DR for developers (what header to set to force variant). Also ask for permission to replay their requests internally for debugging.

Jenna Carter: Customer OK with replay and pinning, they want ETA ~2 hours.

Eli Wang: Doing step 1 now. Applying routing override:```json
{
  "customer_id":"nh-7462",
  "preferred_variant":"redwood-2b",
  "allow_fallback":false,
  "ttl_seconds":7200
}
```

Model-Routing-Bot: [action] override applied for customer nh-7462 -> preferred_variant redwood-2b (no fallback) by eli.wang@redwood (job 4829)
Model-Routing-Bot: [log] replaying req_0249b3 -> redwood-2b -> response matches original non-emergency phrasing
Model-Routing-Bot: [log] replaying req_0249b4 -> redwood-2b -> response matches original non-emergency phrasing

Eli Wang: Replay confirms the inconsistency was due to cross-variant routing. Both replays against pinned redwood-2b return the calmer phrasing.

Kira Nakamura: For RCA: we need to look at two things — (1) quantized variant decode defaults (temperature, penalty settings) might differ, and (2) safety post-processing differences (we have a lightweight safety filter on q8 to reduce compute; it may have different thresholds). I'll run a quick diff on decode params between `redwood-2b` and `redwood-2b-q8`.

Kira Nakamura: Quick findings: `redwood-2b-q8` had `safety_mode: high` disabled to avoid extra latency in fallback path. Also its default `top_p` was 0.92 vs 0.95 on main variant. Those two small differences can nudge outputs across the safety boundary.

Eli Wang: Noted. Why was `safety_mode: high` disabled on q8?

Kira Nakamura: Historical reason: the quantized pipeline has a more brittle postprocess; enabling the strict safety-check caused false positives/latency spikes. We prioritized availability. But enabling `safety_mode` on fallback variants by default is causing output divergence.

Ravi Patel: Action items so far: 
- [Eli] Pin Nimbus traffic for 2h (done) and confirm with customer (ETA: immediate)
- [Kira] Run parameter parity test across variants and produce a short doc of the differences and recommended defaults (ETA: 8h)
- [Eli/Kira] Quick patch to routing: do not route same customer requests to different variants within 15 minutes; prefer variant parity (ETA: 48h for config change)
- [Product/Eng] Review fallback policy used in v2 rollout; rollback the `allow_fallback:true` if it breaks consistency guarantees (Ravi to escalate)

Jenna Carter: Customer updated: pinned and replays look good. They requested a written note for their compliance team explaining what happened and steps we took.

Ravi Patel: I'll assemble the notes and include: timeline, evidence (routing logs), mitigation (pinning), and long-term fix plan. Also include recommended API header to pin variant from the customer side: `x-model-variant: redwood-2b` or use `routing: { "preferred_variant": "redwood-2b" }` in the request body.

Eli Wang: For longer term, propose we: (A) add variant consistency SLO — customer-level sticky routing for at least 15 minutes by default, (B) enforce decode/safety parity across variants we advertise as drop-in replacements, and (C) add a policy flag `no-variant-fallback` customers can set on their account.

Kira Nakamura: I will also run a synthetic test suite across the quantized variants to produce a delta matrix for safety-sensitive prompts. That will help product decide which variants are safe as fallbacks.

Ravi Patel: Customer-facing note draft (short):
"We saw your two requests were routed to two different model variants after our rollout. One variant had slightly different decoding/safety settings which caused divergent phrasing. We've pinned your traffic to the primary variant and replayed your requests — results consistent. We're also implementing routing and config changes to prevent this happening again. Apologies for the broken test; we'll follow up with a compliance note and timeline."

Jenna Carter: Nimbus accepted the message and asked for the compliance note within 24h.

Eli Wang: I'll open an eng-runtime ticket to make the 15-minute sticky default and add `no-variant-fallback` flag. Ticket: ER-2026. Assign Kira and me.

Model-Routing-Bot: [ticket] ER-2026 created by eli.wang@redwood -> ensure variant parity, sticky routing default, and account-level no-fallback flag

Ravi Patel: Great. Closing loop: I'll update the support ticket, attach routing logs and replay outputs, and confirm with customer once ER-2026 is triaged.

Jenna Carter: Thanks all. Pinging @Kira and @Eli for updates in this thread once they have the parity doc. :thumbsup:

Eli Wang: Will update here when the config change is scheduled.

Kira Nakamura: Parity doc draft will be in `#eng-ml` and I'll link here.

-- end of thread --
